blocks.prompt: 7. Find the sum of 20 terms of the series whose \(r^{\text{th}}\) term is \(3r + 1\).
blocks.explanation:
The general term is given as a formula in \(r\).
We must add the first 20 terms.
Plan: find \(a_1\) and \(a_{20}\) from the formula, check it is an A.P., then use \(S_n = \frac{n}{2}(a_1 + a_n)\).
steps:
Given: \(a_r = 3r + 1\).
To find: \(S_{20}\).
Method: A general term of the form \(pr + q\) (linear in \(r\)) always gives an A.P. with \(d = p\). So we only need the first and the 20th terms.

Write the first terms
\[a_1 = 3(1) + 1 = 4\]
\[a_2 = 3(2) + 1 = 7\]
\[a_3 = 3(3) + 1 = 10\]
Why: Put \(r = 1, 2, 3\) in the formula.

Confirm it is an A.P.
\[a_{r+1} - a_r\]
\[= [3(r + 1) + 1] - [3r + 1]\]
\[= 3\]
Why: The difference is the same for every \(r\), so \(d = 3\).

Check another way
\[\sum_{r=1}^{20} (3r + 1)\]
\[= 3(1 + 2 + \dots + 20) + 20\]
\[= 3(210) + 20 = 650 \;\checkmark\]
Why: \(1 + 2 + \dots + 20 = \frac{20 \times 21}{2} = 210\), and the "+1" is added 20 times.
